title: On-disk progress document
description:
## What to build

Add the on-disk progress document so that each sub-issue run accumulates cross-iteration context in `.afk-ralph/progress-<epic-id>.md`, committed alongside the code changes for that sub-issue.

- New `progress-doc.ts` deep module. Interface (names illustrative): `filepath(epicId)`, `ensure(epicId, epicTitle)`, `read(epicId)`, `buildProgressSection(content)`, `formatEntry(issue, status, body)`. Pure file and string manipulation; no beads or GitHub calls.
- Orchestrator: at the start of each iteration, read the progress file (creating it if missing) and inject prior entries into the prompt via a new `progressSection` template variable.
- `prompt-implement-issue.md`: add a step instructing the sub-agent to append its final progress entry (the `**Status:** ... / Did: / Discovered: / For next agent: / Blockers:` block) to `.afk-ralph/progress-<epic-id>.md` as part of its commit, before `git push`. Document that the path is relative to the repo root.
- The file format matches today's Linear document layout: H1 title, short intro, `---` separator, then one `## <id>: <title>` entry per iteration with a timestamped subhead and the sub-agent's body.

## Development approach

Use the `tdd` skill (red-green-refactor) to implement `progress-doc.ts`. Its interface is pure and easy to table-test (see slice #10 for the actual tests).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/afk-ralph/progress-doc.ts` exists with the interface described above.
- [ ] On first run against an epic with no existing progress file, the orchestrator creates `.afk-ralph/progress-<epic-id>.md` with the initial header.
- [ ] On the second iteration within a run (or across runs), the prior entry from the file is present in the injected `progressSection` template variable.
- [ ] `prompt-implement-issue.md` instructs the sub-agent to append its progress entry to the file before pushing.
- [ ] After a successful sub-issue run in code mode, the sub-agent's commit includes the updated progress file.
- [ ] `bun run typecheck` passes.

## User stories addressed

- User story 7
- User story 8

title: Tracer bullet: code mode single-run end-to-end
description:
## What to build

Tracer bullet for the Linear → beads migration. A single end-to-end run of afk-ralph driven by beads, demonstrating that the orchestrator can pick a beads epic, pick one AI-labeled ready child, invoke Claude with the new prompt, and land a PR — with no Linear code paths involved.

Scope for this slice (deliberately minimal — later slices layer on):
- New `bd.ts` typed wrapper with the minimum functions needed: `listOpenEpics`, `showIssue`, `listReadyChildren`. Implemented as `Bun.spawn(["bd", ...])` calls with `--json` parsing and typed return values.
- `index.ts` rewrite: remove the `@linear/sdk` import, `LinearClient` setup, team picker, "assigned to me" filter, `fetchPrdIssues`, `fetchRemainingChildren`, all Linear status/state-map code, all progress-document code (deferred to slice #2). Replace the epic picker with `listOpenEpics()`. Replace the child picker with `listReadyChildren(epic, "AI")`. Iterate exactly one child when run in single mode; multi-child iteration may work but is not required for this slice.
- Branch naming: derive `<bd-id>/<slugified-title>` from the epic's id and title. Slug rules: lowercase, non-`[a-z0-9]` → `-`, runs collapsed, trailing `-` trimmed, capped near 40 chars.
- `prompt-implement-issue.md` rewrite for the new sub-agent contract: the sub-agent claims with `bd update --claim`, implements, runs quality gates, closes with `bd close <id>` (or `bd update <id> --status blocked`), then `git pull --rebase && bd dolt push && git push`. Remove "Do NOT push to git — the orchestrator handles that." Progress-doc append is NOT in this slice; reference only the new bd session-close steps.
- `prompt-pr-body.md` rewrite: describe a "beads epic", drop `{{prdUrl}}` variable and the `Linear:` trailer.
- PR creation/update flow unchanged except for the template vars (no more `prdUrl`).
- Orchestrator does NOT push git (sub-agent owns that now per CLAUDE.md workflow).

Out of scope for this slice (owned by later slices): on-disk progress document, stale in_progress reset, in-review label, post-run status verification, beads comments injection into prompt, Feedback-label PR-thread resolution, investigate-mode prompt update, cosmetic polish (`linear()` → `beads()`, header comment, bd PATH preflight).

## Development approach

Use the `tdd` skill (red-green-refactor) to implement the slug helper if it is extracted as its own function — it's pure string manipulation and trivial to test. Everything else in this slice talks to external systems (beads CLI, git, Claude) and is tested manually by running afk-ralph end-to-end.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/afk-ralph/index.ts` has no `@linear/sdk` import and no references to `LinearClient`, `LINEAR_API_KEY`, team pickers, or assigned-to-me filtering.
- [ ] `src/afk-ralph/bd.ts` exists and exports `listOpenEpics`, `showIssue`, and `listReadyChildren`, each typed and each parsing `bd --json` output.
- [ ] Running `bun run afk-ralph` (or equivalent invocation) with one open epic that has a single AI-labeled ready child successfully: picks the epic, picks the child, checks out branch `<bd-id>/<slug>`, invokes Claude, and on success pushes the branch and opens/updates a PR.
- [ ] `prompt-implement-issue.md` instructs the sub-agent to claim, close or mark blocked, and push (bd + git) per the CLAUDE.md session-close workflow. It does NOT tell the sub-agent to skip pushing.
- [ ] `prompt-pr-body.md` describes a "beads epic", has no `{{prdUrl}}` placeholder, and no `Linear:` trailer.
- [ ] Slug helper produces the same output for these cases (table covered by tests or by a quick manual check — formal tests are in slice #10): empty, all punctuation, mixed-case title, title with emoji, very long title truncated near 40 chars.
- [ ] `bun run typecheck` passes.

## User stories addressed

- User story 1
- User story 2
- User story 3
- User story 10
- User story 17
- User story 22

title: Investigate mode end-to-end
description:
## What to build

Make investigate mode work end-to-end against beads. Primary change is the prompt file; orchestrator wiring is already in place from the tracer bullet.

- `prompt-investigate-issue.md`: replace "If the issue requires updating Linear (creating/editing issues, adding comments, changing labels, etc.), use the Linear MCP tools directly." with an equivalent sentence pointing the sub-agent at the `bd` CLI (`bd create`, `bd update`, `bd comment add`, etc.).
- Keep the rest of the investigate prompt unchanged: no code changes, no git commits, final response structured with `**Status:** / Did: / Discovered: / For next agent: / Blockers:`.
- Verify orchestrator `mode === "investigate"` path works end-to-end: no branch checkout, no push, no PR creation, sub-issue still closed or marked blocked based on the `**Status:**` marker. Orchestrator-side status updates for investigate mode stay with the sub-agent (consistent with code mode).

## Development approach

No TDD needed. Verify manually by running afk-ralph in investigate mode against a sub-issue that asks Claude to read some code and write a finding.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `prompt-investigate-issue.md` references `bd` CLI commands, not Linear MCP tools.
- [ ] Running afk-ralph in investigate mode against a single AI-labeled ready child completes the iteration without checking out a branch, committing, pushing, or opening a PR.
- [ ] On a successful investigate run, the sub-issue is closed (via `bd close`) by the sub-agent, per the usual flow.
- [ ] On a failed / blocked investigate run, the sub-issue is marked `blocked`, not closed.
- [ ] `bun run typecheck` passes.

## User stories addressed

- User story 11
- User story 15

title: Beads comments injected into sub-issue prompt
description:
## What to build

Feed beads comments on the sub-issue into the prompt for that sub-issue, the same way Linear comments were injected before.

- Extend `bd.ts` with `listComments(id)` returning an ordered list of comment bodies (author/time metadata optional).
- Orchestrator: after picking a child, call `listComments(id)` and wire the result into the `issueComments` template variable of `prompt-implement-issue.md` / `prompt-investigate-issue.md`.
- If there are no comments, the section is omitted (same behavior as today).

## Development approach

No TDD needed — thin wiring verified manually by leaving a `bd comment add` on a sub-issue and confirming it shows up in the rendered prompt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bd.ts` exposes `listComments`.
- [ ] On a sub-issue with no comments, the prompt renders without a comments section.
- [ ] On a sub-issue with one or more comments, the comments appear in the rendered prompt under the existing `## Comments` heading, in chronological order.
- [ ] `bun run typecheck` passes.

## User stories addressed

- User story 13

title: Feedback-label PR thread resolution preserved
description:
## What to build

Preserve the existing Feedback-labeled sub-issue flow (reply to the PR review comment, resolve the GitHub review thread) under beads. The label name, the `<!-- afk-ralph-metadata -->` protocol, and the `resolveFeedbackOnGitHub` GitHub API calls all stay. Only the source of the label and description needs to change — read them from the beads issue instead of the Linear issue.

- Confirm `parseFeedbackMetadata` still works on whatever description text beads returns for the sub-issue (it's a simple HTML-comment regex — should be format-agnostic).
- Orchestrator: on successful completion of a sub-issue in code mode, if the sub-issue has the `Feedback` label, run `resolveFeedbackOnGitHub(metadata, commitSha)` exactly as today.
- The `pr-feedback-to-issues` skill that CREATES these Feedback issues is NOT updated in this slice — it remains Linear-backed. This slice just handles resolution on the afk-ralph side.

## Development approach

Use the `tdd` skill for `parseFeedbackMetadata` if you want extra coverage, but it's unchanged from today — a quick manual verification that a Feedback issue with HTML-comment metadata is still parsed correctly under beads is sufficient.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a closed sub-issue has the `Feedback` label, `resolveFeedbackOnGitHub` is invoked with the parsed metadata and the short commit SHA.
- [ ] When a closed sub-issue does NOT have the `Feedback` label, `resolveFeedbackOnGitHub` is NOT invoked.
- [ ] A Feedback-labeled sub-issue whose description contains no `<!-- afk-ralph-metadata -->` comments logs a warning and does not error.
- [ ] `bun run typecheck` passes.

## User stories addressed

- User story 12

title: in-review label on epic when all children closed
description:
## What to build

When the main iteration loop exits because every AI-labeled child of the epic is closed, add the `in-review` label to the epic and `bd dolt push` that change. This is the beads analog of Linear's "In Review" PRD state.

- Extend `bd.ts` with `addLabel(id, label)` and `doltPush()`.
- Orchestrator: after the loop, if all children closed, call `addLabel(epicId, "in-review")` followed by `doltPush()`.
- If the run ends with children still open (e.g., blocked, single-mode exit, or user aborted), do NOT add the label.

## Development approach

No TDD needed — thin wiring verified manually by running afk-ralph on an epic with a single AI-labeled child that completes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bd.ts` exposes `addLabel` and `doltPush`.
- [ ] After a full run where every AI-labeled child ends up closed, the epic has the `in-review` label.
- [ ] `bd dolt push` runs once after the label is added.
- [ ] On a run that exits with children still open, the epic does NOT get the `in-review` label.
- [ ] `bun run typecheck` passes.

## User stories addressed

- User story 9
- User story 23

title: Post-run status verification
description:
## What to build

After each sub-agent run, read `bd show <id> --json` and compare the sub-issue's status to the `**Status:**` marker parsed from the sub-agent's final output. If they disagree, log a warning — but do not abort. This catches a sub-agent that claimed "completed" without actually closing the issue (or vice versa).

- The bd status is treated as the source of truth for orchestrator routing (e.g., whether to add `in-review` at the end).
- The `**Status:**` marker stays useful for the progress-doc entry and for this verification.
- A warning log line identifies the sub-issue, both values, and a short hint to investigate.

## Development approach

No TDD needed — this is a small post-run check verified manually by tweaking the sub-agent prompt to force a mismatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Orchestrator calls `bd show <id> --json` after each sub-agent run.
- [ ] When the `**Status:** completed` marker is present but bd status is not `closed`, a warning is printed identifying the discrepancy.
- [ ] When the `**Status:** blocked` marker is present but bd status is not `blocked`, a warning is printed identifying the discrepancy.
- [ ] When the marker and bd status agree, no warning is printed.
- [ ] The warning is non-fatal — the loop continues.
- [ ] `bun run typecheck` passes.

## User stories addressed

- User story 6

title: Stale in_progress reset at startup
description:
## What to build

At orchestrator startup, after the user picks an epic, find any AI-labeled children of that epic whose status is `in_progress` (left over from a crashed prior run) and reset them to `open` so that `bd ready` can pick them back up cleanly. Log each reset so it's visible in the terminal. `bd dolt push` once after the batch.

- Extend `bd.ts` with `listChildrenByStatus(epicId, label, status)` and `resetStatus(id, status)`.
- Orchestrator: insert the reset step between epic selection and the main iteration loop.

## Development approach

No TDD needed — this is thin wiring over the new `bd.ts` functions, verified manually by deliberately leaving a child in `in_progress` and running afk-ralph.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bd.ts` exposes `listChildrenByStatus` and `resetStatus`.
- [ ] On startup against an epic with one AI-labeled `in_progress` child, the orchestrator flips that child to `open`, logs a one-line message identifying the reset child, and proceeds to `bd ready`.
- [ ] `bd dolt push` runs once after the resets (if any resets happened).
- [ ] With no stale children, no reset log lines appear and no `bd dolt push` runs.
- [ ] `bun run typecheck` passes.

## User stories addressed

- User story 4
- User story 23

title: Convert afk-ralph from Linear to beads
description:
## Problem Statement

afk-ralph's loop orchestrator is hard-wired to Linear. It reads PRDs via `@linear/sdk`, iterates their children, flips Linear workflow states, and writes progress to a Linear document. Beads (`bd`) is now the local issue tracker for this repo — the Linear coupling means afk-ralph cannot drive work tracked in beads without running a second tracker in parallel. I want afk-ralph to iterate a beads epic's AI-labeled children with the same ergonomics it had for Linear PRDs (single command, runs to completion, produces a PR), and I want to drop the Linear dependency entirely from this script.

## Solution

Replace all Linear calls in afk-ralph with `bd` CLI invocations. Model a beads **epic** as the unit of work (what used to be a PRD), model **AI-labeled children** as the sub-issues to iterate, and model a **local on-disk markdown file** as the progress document. Delegate status transitions, commits, and pushes to the sub-agent per the CLAUDE.md session-close workflow; the orchestrator only picks work and handles epic-level bookkeeping plus the PR.

## User Stories

1. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want afk-ralph to list my open beads epics at startup, so that I can pick one to run without leaving the terminal.
2. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want afk-ralph to iterate only AI-labeled children of the chosen epic, so that non-automated sub-issues are never accidentally run through Claude.
3. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want afk-ralph to use `bd ready --parent <epic> --label AI --json` for work selection, so that blocker-aware ordering is handled by beads and not hand-rolled.
4. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want stale `in_progress` children (from a prior crashed run) reset to `open` at startup, so that afk-ralph can re-select them via `bd ready`.
5. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want the sub-agent to claim, implement, commit, update the progress doc, close (or mark blocked), run `bd dolt push`, and `git push` as a single unit per CLAUDE.md, so that there is no drift between the repo state and the beads state.
6. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want the orchestrator to verify each sub-agent's reported status against `bd show <id> --json` after the run, so that a sub-agent claiming "completed" without closing the issue is caught.
7. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want a local progress doc at `.afk-ralph/progress-<epic-id>.md` committed alongside the code for each sub-issue, so that cross-iteration context persists in git history and is readable without tool access.
8. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want prior progress entries injected into the next sub-issue's prompt, so that each sub-agent inherits context from prior iterations.
9. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want the epic labelled `in-review` when all children close, so that I can query epics awaiting human PR review without reinventing a state field.
10. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want the PRD branch named `<bd-id>/<slugified-title>`, so that my branch list groups afk-ralph work under the epic ID.
11. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want "code" and "investigate" modes preserved, so that I retain the non-mutating investigation flow.
12. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want the Feedback-labeled sub-issue flow (reply-to-PR-comment + resolve-thread) preserved unchanged, so that the PR review resolution loop keeps working after the migration.
13. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want beads comments on a sub-issue fed into its prompt, so that human review notes left on the issue reach the sub-agent.
14. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want clickable Linear terminal links dropped in favor of plain `bd-xxx` identifiers, so that output stays honest about the local-only nature of beads.
15. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want the investigate-mode prompt to reference `bd` CLI commands instead of Linear MCP tools, so that the sub-agent knows how to update the tracker it actually has access to.
16. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want the PR body prompt updated to describe the beads epic instead of a Linear PRD (and to drop the Linear URL trailer), so that generated PR descriptions match reality.
17. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want `@linear/sdk` removed from afk-ralph's imports but kept in package.json (since `upload-to-linear` still needs it), so that unrelated scripts keep working.
18. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want a preflight check that `bd` is on `$PATH`, so that the script fails fast with a clear message if beads is not installed.
19. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want the bd-related plumbing in a small typed `bd.ts` wrapper rather than inlined in the main file, so that the orchestrator stays readable and the wrapper can be unit-tested.
20. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want the existing `render-prompt.test.ts` left alone, so that no tangentially related tests break during this migration.
21. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want the ANSI log prefix renamed from `[Linear]` to `[Beads]` with the same magenta color, so that runtime output reflects the new backend.
22. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want "single" vs "afk" run modes preserved, so that I can still iterate one sub-issue at a time when debugging.
23. As a dotfiles maintainer, I want orchestrator-side bd writes (resetting stale `in_progress`, adding `in-review` label) followed by `bd dolt push`, so that orchestrator bookkeeping is visible to anyone syncing the Dolt remote.

## Implementation Decisions

### Modules to build or modify

- **`src/afk-ralph/bd.ts`** (new) — Typed wrapper around `Bun.spawn(["bd", ...])`. Parses JSON output, normalizes errors. Functions (sketch, names illustrative):
  - `listOpenEpics()` → epics with `type=epic`, not closed
  - `showIssue(id)` → full issue record
  - `listReadyChildren(epicId, label)` → `bd ready --parent --label --json`, blocker-aware
  - `listChildrenByStatus(epicId, label, status)` → for the stale-reset step
  - `resetStatus(id, status)` → `bd update <id> --status <status>`
  - `addLabel(id, label)` → `bd update <id> --add-label <label>`
  - `listComments(id)` → `bd comments <id>` content
  - `doltPush()` → `bd dolt push`
- **`src/afk-ralph/index.ts`** (modified) — Remove the entire Linear section (`LinearClient` import, `getLinearClient`, `getStateMap`, `setIssueStatus`, `fetchTeams`, `fetchPrdIssues`, `fetchRemainingChildren`, `progressDocTitle`, `findProgressDocId`, `ensureProgressDoc`, `fetchProgressDocContent`, `updateProgressDocContent`, `appendProgressEntry`, `buildProgressSection`, `RemainingChild` type, `linear()` log helper). Replace with `bd.ts` calls and local filesystem I/O for the progress doc. Rename log helper to `beads()`. Drop "assigned to me" and team-picker prompts. Update the top-of-file `// description:` comment. Remove `LINEAR_API_KEY` check; add `bd` PATH check. Drop clickable terminal `link()` calls around issue IDs.
- **`src/afk-ralph/progress-doc.ts`** (new, optional but recommended deep module) — Owns the on-disk progress file at `.afk-ralph/progress-<epic-id>.md`. Interface: `ensure(epic)`, `read(epicId)`, `buildProgressSection(content)`, `formatEntry(issue, status, body)`, `filepath(epicId)`. Does no bd or Linear work — pure file + string manipulation. Deep: small interface, lots of encapsulated formatting logic.
- **`src/afk-ralph/prompt-implement-issue.md`** (modified) — Instructions rewritten for the CLAUDE.md session-close workflow: claim with `bd update --claim`, implement, run quality gates, append a progress entry to `.afk-ralph/progress-<epic-id>.md`, close with `bd close <id>` (or `bd update <id> --status blocked`), then `git pull --rebase && bd dolt push && git push`. Remove "Do NOT push to git — the orchestrator handles that."
- **`src/afk-ralph/prompt-investigate-issue.md`** (modified) — Replace "use the Linear MCP tools directly" with "use `bd` CLI commands". Keep the no-code-changes / no-commits constraint.
- **`src/afk-ralph/prompt-pr-body.md`** (modified) — Replace "Linear PRD" with "beads epic"; drop the trailing `Linear: {{prdUrl}}` line and the `{{prdUrl}}` template variable.

### Deep-module opportunities

- `bd.ts` encapsulates all `bd` CLI interaction behind typed functions. Main loop never formats a `bd` argv or parses `bd` JSON directly.
- `progress-doc.ts` encapsulates the progress-document format and on-disk location behind a tiny interface; easy to unit-test without a real beads DB or GitHub.

### Architectural decisions

- **Full replacement** (not dual-mode, not a fork). Linear code leaves afk-ralph entirely. `@linear/sdk` stays in `package.json` because `upload-to-linear` uses it.
- **Epic = PRD**, identified by `type=epic`, not by a `PRD` label.
- **AI label** on children is the automation opt-in; unchanged.
- **No "In Review" status** (beads has no such status). Epic gets an `in-review` label when all children close.
- **Branch naming**: `<bd-id>/<slugified-title>` — slug lowercased, non-`[a-z0-9]` → `-`, runs collapsed, trailing `-` trimmed, capped around 40 chars.
- **Progress document**: on-disk markdown at `.afk-ralph/progress-<epic-id>.md`, committed with each sub-issue's code. Sub-agent appends the entry as part of its commit. Orchestrator reads the file to inject prior entries into the next prompt.
- **Division of labor**: sub-agent owns claim → implement → append progress → quality gates → close/blocked → `bd dolt push` → `git push` per CLAUDE.md. Orchestrator owns epic selection, stale-reset, prompt assembly, post-run verification via `bd show`, `in-review` labelling, PR creation/update, Feedback-label PR thread resolution.
- **Stale `in_progress` handling**: reset to `open` at startup so `bd ready` picks them up cleanly.
- **Post-run verification**: orchestrator reads `bd show <id> --json` after each sub-agent run and compares to the parsed `**Status:**` marker. Mismatch is warned (not fatal); `bd` is source of truth.
- **Dolt push cadence**: orchestrator `bd dolt push`es only after its own writes (stale reset, `in-review` label). Sub-agent pushes per CLAUDE.md for its own work.
- **No Linear URL / clickable terminal links**. Issues render as plain `bd-xxx` text.
- **No team picker, no "assigned to me" filter** — beads is local/single-user.

### CLI and prompt flow (end to end)

- Orchestrator at startup: model/effort/mode/run-mode prompts (unchanged) → list open epics → user picks one → derive branch name → checkout branch (code mode only) → ensure progress file exists → reset stale `in_progress` AI-labeled children.
- Each iteration: `bd ready --parent <epic> --label AI --json` → if empty exit loop; else pick top → read progress file → list comments → render prompt → invoke Claude agent query → parse `**Status:**` marker → `bd show <id> --json` to verify → if Feedback label, run `resolveFeedbackOnGitHub` → single-mode breaks here.
- After loop: if all closed, `bd update <epic> --add-label in-review` + `bd dolt push` → in code mode create/update PR (prompt uses epic data, no Linear URL).

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests here describe **external behavior** (what input produces what output) of pure helpers. The live loop talks to beads, git, GitHub, and Claude — all external systems; integration-testing it is out of scope for this PRD.
- **Modules worth testing:**
  - `render-prompt.test.ts` — already exists and covers template rendering; leave as-is.
  - `progress-doc.ts` — worth a small test suite covering: path derivation from epic id; `buildProgressSection` output when doc is empty vs. has entries; `formatEntry` output shape. Fixtures are strings; no mocks needed.
  - A slug helper (for branch names) — worth a table-driven test: empty title, title with emoji/unicode, long title truncation, title with only punctuation, leading/trailing whitespace.
- **Prior art**: `render-prompt.test.ts` is the pattern — `bun:test`, small deterministic inputs, string assertions.
- **Not tested (explicitly out of scope)**: `bd.ts` (thin shell wrapper over a CLI — unit tests would just mock `Bun.spawn` and assert argv shape, low value), the main loop (integration-heavy), the PR and feedback flows (already untested today).
- The user has not yet decided which of the new modules they want formal tests for; at minimum the slug helper and `progress-doc.ts` are recommended.

## Out of Scope

- Updating the `pr-feedback-to-issues` skill to create beads issues instead of Linear issues. That skill is separate and keeps its Linear behavior for now.
- Migrating existing in-flight Linear PRDs into beads. No data migration tool.
- Modifying `upload-to-linear/`; it remains Linear-only.
- Adding a dual-mode / `--tracker=linear|beads` flag to afk-ralph.
- Replacing `@linear/sdk` in `package.json` (other scripts still depend on it).
- Changing `prompt-implement-issue.md` output contract (the `**Status:** completed|blocked` / `Did:` / `Discovered:` / `For next agent:` / `Blockers:` structure stays).
- Changing the Feedback-label / `<!-- afk-ralph-metadata -->` protocol. The GitHub resolution flow is kept bit-for-bit.
- Any change to how Claude is invoked (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` call, allowed tools, maxTurns, etc.).
- Adding an MCP server for beads; orchestrator shells out to the `bd` CLI directly.

## Further Notes

- The sub-agent's prompt will now include instructions that reference paths relative to the repo root (`.afk-ralph/progress-<epic-id>.md`). The agent runs with `cwd: process.cwd()`, which is whatever dir the user invoked afk-ralph from — almost always the repo root. If not, the progress doc path breaks; document that assumption in the prompt.
- Beads' `bd update <id> --claim` sets status to `in_progress` and records the actor. The sub-agent must claim explicitly rather than assuming the orchestrator did it.
- `bd ready` excludes `in_progress` by design. The stale-reset step at orchestrator startup is what re-admits crashed iterations. Any concurrent human work on an AI-labeled sub-issue (rare but possible) would also be reset — this is acceptable because AI-labeled children are meant to be driven by afk-ralph.
- The `in-review` label on the epic is a convention established by this PRD. It doesn't block anything in beads; it's purely for human querying (`bd list --label in-review`) and to leave a footprint once afk-ralph finishes all children.
- The PR creation step still uses the sub-agent (`query`) internally to generate the PR body — that sub-agent only reads `git log`/`git diff`, does not touch beads, and is unaffected by the migration other than the prompt variables it receives.
design:
## Key design calls

- **Full replacement** — no dual-mode, no fork. `@linear/sdk` stays in `package.json` for `upload-to-linear/` but is removed from afk-ralph imports.
- **PRD → epic** via `type=epic`, not a label. AI label kept as the automation opt-in on children.
- **Progress doc lives on disk** at `.afk-ralph/progress-<epic-id>.md`, committed alongside each sub-issue's code by the sub-agent.
- **Branch naming**: `<bd-id>/<slugified-title>`.
- **"In Review" → `in-review` label** on the epic once all children close.
- **Work selection**: `bd ready --parent <epic> --label AI --json` (blocker-aware out of the box).
- **Stale `in_progress` reset** at orchestrator startup so `bd ready` can pick crashed iterations back up.
- **Division of labor**: sub-agent owns claim → implement → progress-doc append → quality gates → close/blocked → `bd dolt push` → `git push` per CLAUDE.md. Orchestrator owns epic picking, stale reset, prompt assembly, post-run verification via `bd show`, `in-review` labelling, PR creation, Feedback-thread resolution.
- **Orchestrator invokes bd** via a typed `bd.ts` wrapper over `Bun.spawn`, parallel to how `git`/`gh` are already shelled out. No beads MCP.
- **Plain-text issue IDs** in terminal output — clickable Linear URL links dropped.
- **Verification**: orchestrator reads `bd show <id> --json` after each run; warns (does not abort) if status and the parsed `**Status:**` marker disagree.
- **Dolt push cadence**: orchestrator pushes only after its own writes (stale reset, `in-review` label). Sub-agent pushes per CLAUDE.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- `src/afk-ralph/index.ts` has no `import { LinearClient ... } from "@linear/sdk"` and no references to `LINEAR_API_KEY`, Linear documents, team picker, or `assignedIssues`.
- `src/afk-ralph/bd.ts` exists and exposes typed wrappers for: listing open epics, `bd show <id>`, `bd ready --parent --label --json`, listing children by status, updating status, adding a label, listing comments, and `bd dolt push`.
- Orchestrator lists open epics (`type=epic`) at startup and lets the user pick one.
- Orchestrator resets any AI-labeled children of the chosen epic stuck in `in_progress` back to `open`, logging each.
- Work selection uses `bd ready --parent <epic> --label AI --json`.
- A progress file at `.afk-ralph/progress-<epic-id>.md` is created on first run for an epic and its content is injected into the next sub-issue's prompt.
- `prompt-implement-issue.md` instructs the sub-agent to claim, append to the progress file, close or mark blocked, and run `git pull --rebase && bd dolt push && git push` — with no instruction telling the sub-agent not to push.
- `prompt-investigate-issue.md` references `bd` CLI commands (not Linear MCP tools).
- `prompt-pr-body.md` describes a "beads epic", has no `{{prdUrl}}` template variable, and no `Linear:` trailer.
- Orchestrator adds an `in-review` label on the epic once all AI-labeled children are closed, then `bd dolt push`es that change.
- The Feedback-labeled PR-thread resolution flow still triggers when the target sub-issue has the `Feedback` label and parses `<!-- afk-ralph-metadata -->` comments from the issue description.
- Orchestrator warns (does not abort) when the `**Status:**` marker in the sub-agent's output disagrees with the bd status after the run.
- Running afk-ralph without `bd` on `$PATH` fails fast with a clear error message.
- Branch used per run is `<bd-id>/<slugified-title>`; slug is lowercase, non-`[a-z0-9]` → `-`, runs collapsed, trailing `-` trimmed, capped near 40 chars.
- `render-prompt.test.ts` still passes unmodified.
- `bun run typecheck` passes after the change.

title: Polish: rename, preflight, headers
description:
## What to build

Pure polish after the core functional slices land.

- Rename the ANSI log-prefix helper from `linear()` (magenta `[Linear]`) to `beads()` (magenta `[Beads]`). Same color, same formatting. Update every call site.
- Update the top-of-file `// description:` comment in `src/afk-ralph/index.ts` from "Run Claude in a loop to complete Linear PRD sub-issues automatically" to something accurate to the new implementation (e.g., "Run Claude in a loop to complete beads epic sub-issues automatically").
- Remove any remaining `LINEAR_API_KEY` env check or related startup assertions.
- Add a preflight check that `bd` is on `$PATH`, mirroring the existing `CLAUDE_PATH` check. On failure, `console.error` with a clear install hint and `process.exit(1)`.
- Drop any remaining clickable terminal link (`\x1b]8;...`) usages that wrap issue IDs. Render IDs as plain text. Clickable links around external HTTP URLs (e.g., the PR URL at the end) stay.

## Development approach

No TDD needed — purely cosmetic and a single startup assertion. Run afk-ralph once to confirm no rendering regressions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] There is no occurrence of `linear(` as a function call in `src/afk-ralph/index.ts` (rename is complete).
- [ ] The `// description:` at the top of `index.ts` no longer says "Linear".
- [ ] No remaining reference to `LINEAR_API_KEY` in `src/afk-ralph/index.ts`.
- [ ] Running afk-ralph without `bd` on `$PATH` exits with a non-zero code and prints a clear error naming `bd`.
- [ ] Issue IDs in terminal output are plain text (no OSC 8 escape sequences around them).
- [ ] `bun run typecheck` passes.
